solutionSql:
WITH scanned AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT id
  FROM staging_scans
  WHERE id IS NOT NULL
    AND status IS NOT NULL
),
runs AS (
  SELECT id, id - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS run_key
  FROM scanned
)
SELECT MIN(id)::integer AS start_id,
       MAX(id)::integer AS end_id,
       COUNT(*)::integer AS scans
FROM runs
GROUP BY run_key
ORDER BY start_id;

rules.howSolved: Only ids with a non-NULL status enter the set, so a status-less or absent id splits the run during the gaps-and-islands step.
SELECT DISTINCT id collapses duplicate ids before the run keys are computed, so a repeated id counts once.

ambiguities: Not stated whether an id sent twice with a status on one copy and no status on the other is a gap; I treated it as having a status (the sample has no such case, and I did not check the hidden datasets).
Not stated what to do with a row that has a NULL id but a status; I excluded it because it cannot be placed in a run.
Not stated whether a blank or whitespace-only status string counts as "no status"; I treated only NULL as no status (the sample has no blank statuses).
notes: Gaps-and-islands with ROW_NUMBER over distinct ids. Ran without error on sample, nulls and boundary. Sample has 5 islands; sample probes found no NULL-id-with-status rows, no duplicate ids with mixed status and no blank statuses. Hidden dataset contents were not inspected.
